issues.claim: §2.7's support step (6) (d) (l. 2607–2609), the home R5-02 wrote this round, makes a wall run laid after a raised way, beneath every non-`vault` span, 'an ordinary run whose top is no higher than that span's soffit (the arch walled up; derived at read, never stored — §4.5's daylight casters, §8.4's casters and heightfield and §11.1's glTF wall read it)'. Its restatements state a different height: §8.4's heightfield writers (l. 13672–13673) and shadow casters (l. 13897–13898) 'a run beneath a raised way's span topped at its soffit'; §11.1's glTF row (l. 15988) 'topped at that span's soffit' and CityJSON row (l. 15989) 'topped at its soffit as in glTF'; §4.5's casters (l. 6150) 'to its soffit'; §7.1's `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` row (l. 10631) 'topped at a span's soffit'; T110-2 (4) (l. 18495–18496) and V06 l. 4170 'topped at its soffit'. R5-02's own summary says 'walled up to a span's soffit'. Where a span's soffit stands above the run's own top, the home gives the run its own height with the arch open above it, and the readers give a run raised to the soffit with the arch filled. This is common: a soffit is at least `clearanceCm` (450 cm for carts, V11 l. 702), and an aqueduct's or a valley viaduct's arches are far taller than a curtain wall. Two builders draw and export different walls, shadow prisms and heightfield tops. No bar separates them: T110-2's and V06's '0 wall runs above a span's soffit' passes both. (6) (d)'s reader list also omits CityJSON's wall objects, which §11.1 now makes read it (repair-r5-rendering's HAND-OFF to model).
issues.required_change: §2.7's support step (6) (d): 'beneath every other span it is an ordinary run whose top is no higher than that span's soffit (the arch walled up; derived at read, never stored — §4.5's daylight casters, §8.4's casters and heightfield and §11.1's glTF wall read it)' → 'beneath every other span it is an ordinary run at its own height, its top cut down to that span's soffit where the soffit is lower — the arch walled up to that top, a run lower than the soffit leaving the arch open above it (derived at read, never stored — §4.5's daylight casters, §8.4's casters and heightfield and §11.1's glTF wall and CityJSON wall objects read it)'. If the adjudicator rules the arch filled to the soffit instead, the home states that for both cases. Each restatement then reads the home's words, citing it. END lines: rendering — §8.4's heightfield writers and shadow casters, and §11.1's glTF and CityJSON clauses, 'a run beneath a raised way's span with its top cut down to that span's soffit where the soffit is lower (§2.7's support step (6) (d))'. pipeline — §4.5's casters (l. 6150). determinism — §7.1's `bend.wall.raisedCrossing` row (l. 10631). scope — T110-2 (4) 'an ordinary run beneath every other span, its top cut down to the span's soffit where the soffit is lower', and its fixture adds 'a span whose soffit stands above the ring's wall top: the run at its own height, the arch open above it'. V06 — l. 4170, in the same words.

issues.claim: §8.2's *The layer* (l. 13180–13185), written this round, puts in each `live.crises` mark's `entity` 'the interned handle (§2.1) of the `ConditionOverlay` whose look draws it'. That column is the one that 'routes deltas, hit-tests, edits' (§8.1 l. 12391). The tile worker's per-tile hit-test slices carry each rastered mark's entity handle (§8.9 l. 14501). §11.2's `HitAnswer` (l. 16362) lists 'every mark under the point … top first by §8.2's draw order … one entry per entity'. V09 §4.20.8 (2) selects 'the top of the stack', and (5) V10's `entity { at }` returns it. `live.crises` is a base layer rastered into the tiles in slot 19b, 'over everything built' (l. 13424), and some of its parts are drawn on buildings and units: marked doors, shutters, scaffolds, the burned farmsteads, a unit's `ruinTone`. No text says whether these marks enter the hit stack. One builder carries their handle into the slices, so a click on a building in a struck unit, or on a siege's camp, selects a `ConditionOverlay`. That is a staged dossier record with no selection, panel or edit route: V09's context panel reads §2.8's entity registry, and the crisis card opens only from the legend, Find's list or the Show menu (V09 §4.21.12 (5)). The clerk's `entity { at }` then names the condition. Another builder leaves view data out of the slices and selects the building. This is a common path whenever a crisis look stands. Before this round, `entity` was unstated for these marks.
issues.required_change: §8.2's *The layer*, after '… and framing their box.', adds: 'The handle serves that reading only: §8.9's hit-test slices leave `live.crises`' marks out, so a click, §11.2's `HitAnswer` and V10's `entity { at }` reach what lies beneath them (V09 §4.20.8).' §8.9's slices row (l. 14501) adds after 'per-tile hit-test slices (mark bboxes + entity handles' the words ', `live.crises`' marks excepted (§8.2)'. T-ER-27 adds the input 'a click on a building, a plot and a camp mark under a standing look' with the outcome 'no crisis mark in the hit stack: the building, the plot, and under a camp what lies beneath it selected', and its bar adds '0 crisis marks in any hit stack'.

issues.claim: R5-04 ('a building never decayed draws its plan unchanged only when no disaster look stands over it') is written at §6.3 *Plan damage* (l. 10010–10011) and §8.6 (l. 14157–14159: 'A building never decayed and under no disaster look draws byte-identically to its plan without the layer (`item123.damage`; T123-7)'), and §2.6 step 7 carries it. A never-decayed building a disaster look stands over draws item 123's layer at the row's `lookLevel` (§8.6 l. 14153–14156; §10.2 (d)). The test §8.6 cites still states the unconditioned rule. T123-7 (§13.2 l. 18718–18720) reads 'a never-decayed building keeps its plan byte for byte as it is without item 123 (the pin `item123.damage` …)'. V12 scopes that pin to 'the buildings whose lineage never held `abandoned`, `decayed` or `ruined`' (l. 933; l. 2761–2763 'every building whose lineage never held …'), which includes a never-decayed building under a disaster look. V12 registers the pin on V03's damage fixtures (T-V3-39 (g), V03 l. 2906: 'a never-decayed building draws, exports and answers byte-identically to its plan without the layer'), and those fixtures hold a disaster district (V03 l. 3260; T-V3-40 (f)). V04 l. 2962, V04's UE33 E1 (l. 2428), V11 l. 3828 and V11 l. 4649 restate the same unconditioned form. R5-04's sweep did not list them, though R5-01 (2) (c) puts the tests in the sweep. The set states two outcomes for one case (the look's damage, or byte-identical), and the pin's bar fails a correct build on a fixture with a struck district.
issues.required_change: T123-7 reads '(T123-7) a never-decayed building under no disaster look (§6.3 *Plan damage*) keeps its plan byte for byte as it is without item 123 (the pin `item123.damage`, a `NoOpPin` of kind `entityScope`)'. END lines: V12 — l. 933's `entities` 'the buildings whose lineage never held `abandoned`, `decayed` or `ruined` and over which no disaster look stands at the drawn week (§10.2 (f))', and l. 2761–2762 the same. V03 — T-V3-39 (g) 'a never-decayed building under no disaster look draws, exports and answers byte-identically to its plan without the layer'. V04 — l. 2962 and UE33 E1 'a building never decayed and under no disaster look'. V11 — l. 3828 and l. 4649 'a building never decayed (level 0) and under no disaster look draws its plan unchanged'.

issues.claim: This round's VRC4T-01 fix makes §8.8 (l. 14380–14383) apply a device-pixel-ratio change 'while the view is settled — at once when no gesture runs, at the gesture's settle otherwise — and at most once in 10 s, counted with the loop's changes, so one coming within 10 s of the last change applies when those 10 s end'. That is R4-10's one phrase 'wherever Auto's or a device-pixel-ratio change's timing is stated', and T-ER-26 now runs the case. V09 still states that timing without the clause. §4.21.11 (2) (l. 3595–3597) reads 'A change takes effect while the view is settled — at once when no gesture runs, at the gesture's settle otherwise — never during a pan, zoom or drag (§8.8)'. T-V9-84 (l. 4435), the test that takes T121-7, reads 'a device-pixel-ratio change re-evaluates within one frame and the level changes while the view is settled — at once when no gesture runs, at the gesture's settle otherwise (§8.8; T121-7)'. For a monitor change with the view idle within 10 s of a loop step-down, §8.8 and T-ER-26 apply it when the 10 s end, while V09's text and bar apply it at once. This is two units stating two outcomes for one case (R5-01's grading), and R5-01 (2) (b) puts V09's restatements in the sweep. R4-10's END texts for these two sites were written before §8.8 stated the within-10-s outcome.
issues.required_change: V09 §4.21.11 (2): '… at the gesture's settle otherwise — never during a pan, zoom or drag (§8.8)' → '… at the gesture's settle otherwise — never during a pan, zoom or drag, and a change Auto's loop decides or a device-pixel-ratio change brings at most once in 10 s, counted together, so one coming within 10 s of the last applies when those 10 s end (§8.8)'. T-V9-84: '… the level changes while the view is settled — at once when no gesture runs, at the gesture's settle otherwise (§8.8; T121-7)' → '… the level changes while the view is settled — at once when no gesture runs, at the gesture's settle otherwise — and at most once in 10 s, so a monitor change within 10 s of a loop step-down applies once those 10 s have passed (§8.8; T121-7)'.

issues.claim: §11.2's `looks` query (l. 16337–16338) takes `building?: Id` and, new this round, `field?: Id`, and `LooksAnswer.crises[].over` (l. 16385) answers 'with the query's building …; with the query's field …'. Neither the members' comments nor the answer say what is returned for a `building` that names no building (an unknown address, a district, a plot, a field) or a `field` that names no field. V10 defines this case only for its own projection of this answer ('absent where the read's building names no building', V10 l. 1025; §3.23 row 34), but the answer's home is §11.2. A script or bridge caller of `query` could get an error, `over` false or no `over`. This is off the common path, since V09 passes a selected building.
issues.required_change: `LooksAnswer.crises[].over`'s comment adds '; absent on every look where the query's building names no building, or its field no field (an unknown address or another kind), every other member as without it — never an error (V10 §3.23 row 34)'. T-ER-27 adds the input 'a `looks` query whose building names a district and whose field names a plot' with the outcome '`over` absent on every look, the rest as without them'.
